message.content:
One of the most iconic sculptures of the 19th century is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Thinker”** (originally part of his monumental *Gates of Hell* project, completed in the 1880s). Although the bronze casts that are most famous today were made in the early 20th century, the original marble version was finished in 1880–1881 and quickly became emblematic of modern sculpture.  

Other highly celebrated 19th‑century works include Rodin’s *The Kiss* (1889), *The Burghers of Calais* (1889), and *The Gates of Hell* (a series of sculptures begun in 1880). These pieces helped define the era’s artistic direction and remain central to discussions of 19th‑century sculpture.
